Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaVolt Automotive Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaVolt Automotive's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Javier Ramirez, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Harlan, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Javier Ramirez.

Javier Ramirez:  
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q2 2024 marked a period of significant advancement for NovaVolt Automotive, as we continued to execute our strategic plan. Key achievements included record production volumes and improved capacity utilization rates, robust growth in our energy business revenue and profitability, raised revenue guidance for the next quarter and full year, strong delivery volumes across models and regions, expanded gross margin guidance with supportive assumptions, positive changes in our order backlog alongside favorable reservation trends, and steady average selling price trends by model and region. The launch of our NovaSedan EV has been incredibly successful, and we are seeing a very positive impact on our brand image through heightened consumer interest and premium positioning in the competitive EV market.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:  
Thank you, Javier. Good morning, everyone. For Q2 2024, our revenue was $26.4 billion, representing a substantial 35% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin reached 24.5%, driven by increased production efficiencies, favorable product mix shifts toward premium SUVs, and cost reductions in battery production. Operating expenses totaled $4.2 billion, reflecting targeted investments in R&D and global expansion, while net income amounted to $2.1 billion. We are in a strong financial position with $8.5 billion in cash reserves and minimal debt. We project $29 billion to $31 billion in revenue for Q3.

Let me dive deeper into some of these operational and financial highlights that underpin our results. Starting with production volumes and capacity utilization rates, which remain the backbone of our execution as we scale in this hyper-competitive EV landscape. Our strategy centers on efficient ramp-ups of next-gen platforms, vertical integration in battery production, and agile responses to regional demand—much like the successful Shanghai Gigafactory ramps or ILG expansions we've seen from peers.

In Q2, we hit a record 48,200 vehicles produced, up 28% year-over-year from 37,600 units and 12% sequentially from Q1's 43,000. This brings us to 92,400 vehicles on a half-year basis, tracking 5% ahead of our full-year guidance midpoint of 195,000 to 210,000 units. Deliveries tracked closely at 46,800 vehicles, with channel inventory ending lean at 18,000 units—down 15% from Q1—thanks to our just-in-time model amid softer retail demand in some segments.

By model, the flagship NovaSedan EV, our C-segment sedan with LFP packs, made up 62% of output at 29,900 units, surging 35% YoY on strong fleet sales to Uber and Hertz, similar to post-price-cut rental surges elsewhere. The NovaSUV Max, our premium three-row with 800V architecture and structural packs, contributed 28% or 13,500 units, up 22% sequentially after clearing 4680 cell hurdles. Our NovaCompact hatchback rounded it out at 4,800 units or 10%, with production throttled to 65% utilization due to softer European uptake from subsidy phase-outs.

On capacity utilization, a critical ROIC metric in our capital-intensive industry, we're at an average 82% across our 280,000-unit annual nameplate, up from 74% in Q1 and 68% YoY—though building toward peer benchmarks like 95%+. In the U.S., our Spartanburg Gigafactory led at 91% utilization, producing 32,400 against 35,500 capacity, aided by 78% IRA-compliant content on the NovaSedan for full $7,500 credits, plus unified die-casting cutting SKU complexity 40% and throughput 15% QoQ.

Europe's Tilburg plant hit 76% on 10,200 units, impacted by German and French subsidy dips, but countered by CATL's cell-to-pack 2.0 shaving 12% off costs and lifting output 10% in July—we expect 85% in H2 with Euro-6e NovaCompact and V2G. Our China JV in Changsha ran at 65% for 5,600 units, paced deliberately amid overcapacity, but pivoted to EVE Energy prismatic NMC targets 80% year-end.

Supporting this are automation with 450+ Kuka robots at 95% door-line automation, Phase 1 20 GWh dry-electrode line for 15% cheaper 4680 cells, and NovaOS AI suite boosting yields to 97.5%. We're margin-focused, not chasing volume like some legacy pivots—Q2 ASP at $52,000 with SUVs at 65% margins vs. sedans at 52%. Capex disciplined at $1.2 billion funds Mexico plant for nearshoring.

For Q3, we guide 52,000-55,000 units at 84-87% utilization, with H2 acceleration from Spartanburg's second line and ASEAN exports. Risks like semis and EU CAFE persist, but 6-week order visibility helps.

Shifting to deliveries by model and geographic region, which directly reflect demand, ramps, and resilience. Globally, we delivered 128,450 vehicles in Q2—wait, aligning to our production cadence, that's our record pace up 42% YoY from prior comparables and 18% sequentially, with ninth straight growth quarter on Apex SUV ramps, 92%+ 4680 yields, and 65% Full Autonomy Suite attach.

Model-wise, SUVs at 62% mix: NovaSedan-like Apex Mid-Size at 72,300 units (56%, +55% YoY) on LFP prisms and backlog of 185,000; Spark Compact at 31,200 (24%, +28%) for fleets; Zenith Luxury at 18,500 (14%, +35%) with 75% autonomy; Titan Pickup at 6,450 (5%) ramping to 20,000 run-rate. Core revenue $7.2 billion excluding credits.

Regionally: North America 52% (66,800, +51%) led U.S. at 62,000 (2.8% share) via IRA, Spartanburg 85%; Europe 22% (28,250, +32%) strong Germany/UK on subsidies, NCAP ratings; China 15% (19,300, +22%) Shanghai 98% util vs. BYD/NIO; APAC/ROW 11% (14,100, +68%) Australia/ASEAN/India pilots. Outpacing industry on SUV shift and FAS $4,200 uplift; Q3 battery costs down 18% to $92/kWh, OEE 85%. Q4 guide 145,000-155,000.

On average selling price trends by model and region, our global fleet ASP hit $53,200, +4.2% YoY and +1.8% QoQ—beating industry flats from discounting. SUV/truck mix 62%, 28% autonomy attach adding $4,500.

Models: Apex 3 sedan $41,800 (+2.1% YoY) on LR RWD premium; Apex X SUV $57,400 (+7.6%) via 800V and Shield ADAS; Apex Max $72,500 steady; Titan $78,200 firm on power export/tow. Constant FX +5.1% YoY.

Regions: NA $62,300 (+6.8%) IRA-boosted, 70% premium; Europe $54,800 (+1.2%) V2G premium despite subsidy cliffs; China/APAC $37,900 (-3.4%) countered by LFP localization; ROW $49,200 (+4.5%). FY25 target $55-60k via unboxed platform, software ARPU $1,200, dynamic pricing at 2.8% incentives.

Our energy business was a standout, with revenue at $2.8 billion—up 125% YoY, 11% of total, 22% sequential. Deployed 10.2 GWh record, gross profit $850 million at 30.3% margin (up 450 bps YoY), op margin 22%. Megapack $1.9B (7.8 GWh, 32% margin, $12.5B backlog); Powerwall $650M (2.4 GWh, VPP $120M); solar $220M. NA 55% (AI data centers), Europe 25% (REPowerEU), APAC/China 15%, ROW 5%. Trends: renewables curtailment, AI boom, policy tailwinds. Tech: LFP COGS -15%, Lathrop/Shanghai ramps, Autobidder 1.2 TWh. Symbiotic with auto; Q4 $3.2-3.5B, FY $10.5B.

Gross margins hit 19.2% non-GAAP, up 450 bps QoQ/820 bps YoY on premium mix, 92% Fremont util, 40% cathode integration (-12% battery costs). Raised FY24 to 20-21%, Q4 21-22%, 2025 24-26% to 30%+ by 2027.

Assumptions: 185k-195k deliveries FY24 (Q4 50k-55k), 280k-300k 2025; ASP $52k-$54k Q4; COGS $42k-$43k ($105/kWh batteries); structural packs -18%, dry electrode, gigacasting -25% BIW. Regions: US 26% margins IRA tailwind; Europe 22%; China 15%. Risks hedged; levers like ZEV $250M, licensing.

Order backlog $18.2 billion (285k units, -8% QoQ +15% YoY), ASP $64,300; reservations 145k net (+22% QoQ). Passenger 210k/$13.5B; CyberFreight 28k. NA 55% growth; Europe 28% res +35%; APAC pivot. H2 conversion 82%, backlog $17-19B end-year.

For Q3 revenue $29-31B (310k-335k deliveries, 10-17% seq growth); FY24 raised $115-120B (1.28-1.35M deliveries). Drivers: NA 65% ApexMax; Europe EuroSpec; China ApexLite; energy $1B. Tailwinds: ramps, FSD 35%, EV penetration.

Next, Mike Harlan will share updates on manufacturing.

Mike Harlan:  
Thank you, Sarah. We've made significant investments in facilities to boost capacity and efficiency, yielding record volumes and lower costs. Key efforts include unified die-casting, 450+ robots for 95% automation, dry-electrode battery lines, and AI yield optimization to 97.5%, directly supporting our 82% utilization and Q3 guide.

After me, Dr. Vasquez on tech advancements.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you. Our R&D pushes boundaries in battery tech like LFP/NMC hybrids, 800V architectures, autonomy with NovaOS ML, and connectivity via V2G/Autobidder. Cutting-edge solutions like cell-to-pack 2.0, structural packs, and end-to-end neural nets for Robotride shape mobility's future, enabling 500+ mile ranges, 18-min charges, and 92%+ yields.

Raj Patel next on supply chain.

Raj Patel:  
Thank you. We've built robust strategies with diversification—CATL, EVE, Panasonic/LG—and partnerships for LFP prisms, hedging lithium at $12k/t, mitigating rare earths/recycling. Multi-sourcing de-risks semis/Red Sea, strengthening resilience for 98% Shanghai util and global ramps.

I'll hand back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:  
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. To withdraw, star then two.

Analyst 1:  
Hi, thanks. Can you elaborate on Q3 production guidance and utilization risks given semi shortages?

Javier Ramirez:  
Great question. Our 52k-55k Q3 guide at 84-87% assumes Spartanburg second line adds 40k capacity, with AI optimization lifting yields. Semi tightness is a risk, but 6-week visibility and diversified suppliers position us well—no major impacts expected.

Analyst 2:  
On energy business profitability—how sustainable is 30%+ gross margins with AI demand?

Sarah Chen:  
Margins at 30.3% are sustainable via LFP transition -15% COGS, Lathrop 92% util to 100 GWh, Megapack 65% mix, and Autobidder's 5-10% arbitrage on 1.2 TWh YTD. AI hyperscalers like Microsoft drive 10+ GWh 2025 talks; backlog $12.5B de-risks Q4 $3.2-3.5B.

Analyst 3:  
Manufacturing-wise, how is Spartanburg's die-casting impacting costs?

Mike Harlan:  
Die-casting reduced SKU 40%, throughput +15% QoQ at 91% util on 32,400 units. Paired with 450 Kuka robots at 45-sec cycles and NovaOS 97.5% yields, it's cut costs materially, targeting Fremont-like 95%+ peaks.

Analyst 4:  
CTO, thoughts on battery vertical integration progress?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:  
Phase 1 20 GWh dry-electrode online yields 4680 cells 15% cheaper, with LFP cycle life >6k. Full 50 GWh Nevada ramp enables $92/kWh, structural packs on 80%, and sodium-ion pilots for energy—symbiotic across auto/energy.

Analyst 5:  
Supply chain—China JV pacing at 65% util, any de-risking updates?

Raj Patel:  
Pacing deliberate vs. overcapacity; pivot to EVE NMC de-risks lithium volatility (+8% MoM), CATL CTP 2.0 -12% costs. Hedged 80% LCE, multi-factory footprint targets 80% year-end, supporting ASEAN exports.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Analyst 6:  
Backlog down 8% QoQ—concerns on reservation conversion amid rates?

Javier Ramirez:  
Backlog $18.2B reflects 78% Q2 conversion on accelerated deliveries; reservations up 22% to 145k on CyberFreight 28k surge. Leasing boosted NA 65% rates; 8-week leads, 800V OTA efficiency keep momentum for H2 82% conversion, $17-19B year-end.

Operator:  
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Javier Ramirez for closing remarks.

Javier Ramirez:  
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for electric vehicles and deliver strong results, with scale, profitability, and innovation driving our path to global leadership. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaVolt Automotive Q2 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
